name: Bonaco
body:
BONACO
CR 3

This strange beast is roughly the size of a brown-reddish bull, but with a deerlike head and a long mane on its neck. Its horns are long and curved backwards. As soon as it sees you it turns its back to run, and a strange odor begins to fill the air.

XP 800
N Large magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +6

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 11, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +4 natural, -1 size)
hp 30 (4d10+8)
Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +2
Defensive Abilities corrosive trail; Immune acid

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee slam +6 (1d6+3)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks corrosive feces (60 ft. line, DC 14, 2d6 acid)

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 14, Con 15, Int 4, Wis 13, Cha 4
Base Atk +4; CMB +11 (+13 with overrun); CMD 23 (25 vs. overrun, 27 vs. trip)
Feats Endurance, Improved Overrun, Run B
Skills Acrobatics +7, Perception +6

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Corrosive Feces (Su)

A bonaco’s feces are acidic and consume everything they touch. The beast can direct a spray of its excrements against enemies and pursuers. Treat this as a breath weapon.

Corrosive Trail (Su)

While running, a bonaco can leave a trail of feces 3 feet wide behind itself that lasts for 1 round before losing its acidic power. Creatures that start their turn adjacent to the corrosive trail take 1d6 points of acid damage.

Creatures that start their turn within the trail take 1d6+3 acid damage. If a creature moves into an area of the corrosive trail multiple times in a round, it takes this damage each time it enters its area. A bonaco can leave a corrosive trail for 10 rounds per day at maximum. These rounds need not be consecutive.

ECOLOGY

Environment any hills or plains
Organization solitary, pair, or family (2-4)
Treasure none

A bonaco is a timid beast that lives in the fields and tries to avoid contact with humans and other sentient races.

Its horns cannot be used for a gore attack due to their strange reversed curve. When it sights hunters, a bonaco’s first reaction is to run and protect its flight with a jet of its corrosive feces. It only resorts to physical combat if cornered and fighting for its life.

Usually, there’s no point in hunting a bonaco, except when a panicked creature causes trouble in a town or field.

In these cases, pursuers just try to scare the bonaco off and avoid chasing it for more than necessary.

Bonaco meat is not fit for consumption and could be mildly poisonous. Its pelt can be harvested and used to make a hide armor of acid resistance, though the lingering stink lowers its market value to 2/3 and so it’s not a good deal for an armorer trying to sell their products.
